My values are: x ($74) > z ($69) > w ($68) > y ($61).

However, I also know I have high priority at w and y (rank 1), and lower priority at x and z (rank 2). Since most applicants seem to favor y > x > w > z, it's likely that my Obtainable Schools will consist of w and y, or perhaps w, y, and one of x or z. It's unlikely that x or z would be the *only* schools I can get, given my high priority at w and y and the preferences of other applicants.

Given this, I should rank my schools to maximize my value *within* the likely set of obtainable schools. This means x should be first, then z, then w, then y. Even if I only get w and y, I still want to rank them according to my values, just in case.

Therefore, I will rank x > z > w > y.
